title: The robe not passed on
hookLine: Huineng said the robe would no longer be handed down; the teaching itself is the proof

lines: A SIGN THE LINE GOES ON.
cards: Some families have one object that matters more than anything else in the house. A watch. A ring.

A recipe card in a grandmother's handwriting. It's meant to be handed down, a sign that the line goes on. And some families know the other side of that story: the cousins who stopped speaking over who got the watch.

The thing meant to hold the family together became the thing it split over. Chan had an object like that too: a robe, handed from teacher to student. And in the Platform Sutra, someone decides it should stop.

teach.b: After the two verses on the wall, the sutra says, Hongren calls Huineng in secret, teaches him, and hands him the robe and bowl as the sign of the teaching.
He tells him to leave that same night and go south, because people may try to harm him. And he says, in paraphrase: the robe has become a cause of strife. Let it stop with you.
Monks set off after Huineng to take the robe back.

teach.h: A CHASE TO THE MOUNTAIN PASS.
teach.b: One of them, a former military officer named Huiming, catches up at a mountain pass. Huineng lays the robe on a rock and steps aside. In the sutra, Huiming tries to pick it up and cannot lift it.
Then he says: I came for the teaching, not for the robe. And Huineng gives him one, in paraphrase: not thinking of good, not thinking of evil, right at this moment, what is your original face?
Huiming, the sutra says, awakens on the spot. The man who ran up a mountain for a piece of cloth goes home with something nobody can carry off.
Late in the sutra, near the end of his life, Huineng tells his students the robe will not be handed down.
The proof that the teaching is alive won't be an object anyone can fight over. It will be the teaching itself, showing up in the people who practice it.
The robe stops here, so that the teaching doesn't have to.

how: Zen and Chan schools speak of the teaching passing from teacher to student, often called mind-to-mind transmission, and the story of Huiming at the mountain pass is often retold, with 'original face' used as a koan.

games.q: what does “the robe not passed on” mean?
o: the strife-causing robe stopping with Huineng
a robe kept hidden until a worthy heir appears
a monk's vow to wear only borrowed robes

games.q: the robe not passed on: tap the pairs.
p: chased him to a mountain pass

s: Hongren gave Huineng the robe at a public ceremony
the sutra says he gave it in secret, at night, and sent him south the same night.
the monk who chased Huineng ended up asking for the teaching instead
Huiming said he came for the teaching, not the robe, and was given a question.
in the sutra, the robe keeps being handed down after Huineng
Huineng tells his students it will not be handed down; the teaching is the proof.

games.q: you're Huineng. a monk has chased you up a mountain to take back the robe. what do you do?
o: lay the robe on a rock and step aside
games.why: Huineng set it down. in the sutra Huiming couldn't lift it, and asked for the teaching instead.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you know how to do that could never be handed over in a box: how to apologize properly, how to wait for the bread to rise, how to sit with someone who's grieving.
Notice where it lives, in the hands, in the timing, in the voice. Nobody could lay it on a rock, and nobody could carry it off.

wordCard.voice: The robe not passed on. In the Platform Sutra, the robe that had become a cause of strife stops with Huineng, and the teaching itself carries on. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese (yibo): 'robe and bowl', the sign of the teaching Hongren gave Huineng.

carryVoice: Your line: the robe stops here. The cloth stayed put; the teaching kept walking. I'll be here tomorrow.
